 Coram : Manish Pitale And
 Shreeram V. Shirsat, Jj.
Date : 5th February 2026 P.C. :
. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Agp for respondent Nos.1, 2 and
4 to 6, as also learned counsel appearing for respondent No.3-Municipal Council.

2. This petition was filed by the petitioners, seeking the following reliefs :
"A] That, this Hon'ble Court be pleased to issue writ of mandamus or writ nature of
mandamus or any other appropriate writ direction order thereby directing the
Municipal Council Baramati not to take forcible possession of the suit property
sought to be acquired by the Respondent Municipal Council for the proposed road in
the development plan being road from Nira road to Jamdar road, which is a 24 meter
wide road, without following the due process of law and granting compensation to
the Petitioners under the provisions of Right to Fair compensation Act, 2013.
bipin prithiani 30-wp-7653.23.doc
B] That, this Hon'ble Court be pleased to issue writ of mandamus or writ in the nature of mandamus or any other appropriate writ Gaurav Sameer Phadtare And Anr vs State Of Maha.

1 direction order thereby directing the Respondent Municipal Council that in case it proposes to acquire the property of the Petitioners, then the Corporation cannot insist that they will pay only TDR and not compensation to the Petitioners whose property is being acquired and be pleased to direct the Respondent Municipal Council to pay compensation to the Petitioner in lieu of the suit property being acquired."

3. The respondent No.3-Municipal Council in its affidavit in reply has specifically stated as follows :
"12.
I say and submit that no work of the proposed road has been commenced forcibly on the said land.

The process of demarcation for ascertaining the exact extent and location of the land proposed to be acquired in respect of the affected area is in progress, and there is no intention on the part of Baramati Municipal Council,
Baramati, to carry out forcible land acquisition in any manner whatsoever.

* * * *
14. Since the Municipal Council does not intend to take over the possession of lands which form the subject matter of the Petition, the apprehension expressed by the Petitioners is unfounded and the petition deserves to be disposed off.

The subject lands will be taken over only after proper process of acquisition thereof is carried out as per law."
4. A perusal of the above quoted statements made in the affidavit in reply filed on behalf of the respondent No.3-Municipal Council, addresses the grievance raised on behalf of the petitioners and indicates that forcible possession of the subject land will not be taken and that, if at all, the Municipal Council intends to acquire the land, proper process in accordance with law shall be followed.

Therefore, relief sought in prayer clause (A) is already bipin prithiani 30-wp-7653.23.doc satisfied on the basis of the above quoted statements made in the affidavit in reply filed on behalf of respondent No.3.
The said statements are treated as undertakings given to this Court.

5. As regards the prayer clause (B) quoted hereinabove, we find that the position of law is clarified by a Full Bench of this Court in the case of Shree Vinayak Builders and Developers, Nagpur vs. State of Maharashtra & Ors., 2022 (4) Mh.L.J. 739.

entities.text: Shree Vinayak Builders and Developers, Nagpur vs. State of Maharashtra & Ors., 2022 (4) Mh.L.J. 739
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the said judgment, question No.1 was considered as follows :
"(i) Whether the modes of acquisition provided under section 126(1)(a) and (b) of the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966 are at the choice of either of the parties or only of the acquiring authority?"

entities.text: Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
6. The said question was answered by the Full Bench of this Court in the following manner :
"Question (1) - This Court holds that the acquisition under section 126(1)(a) and (b)
of the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966 has to be consensus Gaurav Sameer Phadtare And Anr vs State Of Maha.

between both the parties and not only at the option of the Acquiring Authority."

8. It is amply clear from the aforesaid view adopted by the Full Bench of this Court that if at all compensation is to be paid to the petitioner by way of Transferable Developers Rights (TDR), it can be done only by consent i.e. only on the basis of an agreement between the petitioners and the respondent No.3-Municipal Council and not otherwise.
9.

Considering the said position of law, it is made clear that as regards prayer clause (B), the compensation in terms of TDR bipin prithiani 30-wp-7653.23.doc would be given to the petitioners,
only if they agree for the same and not otherwise.
10. The writ petition is disposed of in above terms.
11. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.

(SHREERAM V. SHIRSAT, J.) (MANISH PITALE, J.)
